entities.name: Query protein 768 aa
observations: The sequence is 768 aa long, approximately 83.7 kDa, with predicted pI 5.33 and net negative charge at pH 7.
The N-terminal ~500 aa is highly charged, low-complexity, and rich in serine, acidic residues, lysine/arginine, and proline, consistent with a regulatory or disordered region.
The C-terminal region contains a strong Pfam ThrE domain match at residues 527–767 (PF06738.19), corresponding to a multipass membrane transporter-like domain.
The sequence has 100% identity and full query coverage to UniProt Q6CLI2, annotated as pheromone-regulated membrane protein 10 in Kluyveromyces lactis.
The sequence has 46–53% identity over 74–86% of the query to related fungal pheromone-regulated membrane protein 10 homologs, all annotated as multipass membrane proteins with transporter activity.
The architecture supports a fungal membrane transporter or transporter-associated pheromone-response protein; exact substrate and transport mechanism are not established by sequence alone.

entities.name: Pheromone-regulated membrane protein 10
observations: UniProt Q6CLI2 from Kluyveromyces lactis is a reviewed homolog with 100% identity and 100% query coverage to the analyzed sequence; it is annotated as a membrane, multipass membrane protein with transmembrane transporter activity.
Related reviewed homologs Q754J7 and C5E109 from filamentous/yeast fungi show 46–53% identity and are likewise annotated as multipass membrane proteins with transporter activity.
